related_questions.question: What are the new travel requirements?

text_blocks.snippet: Starting May 7, 2025, U.S. travelers will need a REAL ID or an acceptable alternative for domestic flights. This means a REAL ID-compliant driver's license or another form of identification like a passport will be required at airport security checkpoints. Additionally, travelers to the UK need to register for an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA), and those going to Europe will need ETIAS authorization.
snippet_highlighted_words: U.S. travelers will need a REAL ID or an acceptable alternative for domestic flights

list.snippet: Requirement: U.S. travelers need a REAL ID-compliant driver's license or another acceptable form of ID (like a passport) for domestic flights.
What is REAL ID? It's a driver's license or state ID with enhanced security features, often indicated by a star on the ID.
Where to get it? You'll need to visit your state's DMV to obtain a REAL ID.

text_blocks.snippet: Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) for the UK:

list.snippet: Requirement: U.S. and European travelers to the UK need to register for an ETA.
What is it? ETA is an authorization for inbound travelers, modeled after the U.S. ESTA, to streamline border entry and enhance security.
Application: Apply via the UK government's official website or the ETA app.

list.title: Requirement:
list.snippet: U.S. passport holders will need to apply for ETIAS before traveling to most European countries.

list.title: What is it?
list.snippet: ETIAS is a travel authorization for visa-exempt travelers entering Europe for short stays.

list.title: Validity:
list.snippet: Valid for multiple entries for three years or until the passport expires, whichever comes first.

list.title: Passports:
list.snippet: Passports are still valid for international travel and can also be used for domestic flights if they are REAL ID compliant.

list.title: Contact Tracing:
list.snippet: For flights to the U.S., passengers may need to provide contact information for potential contact tracing by public health officials.

list.title: Biometric Data:
list.snippet: Travelers entering EU countries should be prepared for biometric data collection at border crossings.

list.title: Airline Refunds:
list.snippet: Airlines are now required to automatically refund passengers for canceled flights or major schedule changes.

list.title: Baggage:
list.snippet: Passengers can also get refunds for delayed baggage and for services like in-flight WiFi that don't work.
